description: Campos-Vázquez and Medina-Cortina, in Demography (2019), found people in the lightest skin colour category have on average 1.4 additional years of schooling and 53% higher hourly earnings than their darkest-skinned counterparts.
energy_note: Fifty-three per cent, for the shade of his skin.

aspect: EXAMPLE - and it is a mobility effect, not just a level
description: Research on regional variance found that in every region analysed, the lightest-skinned group has a consistent advantage in upward social mobility. Villarreal (2010) found darker skin tones carry higher poverty risk and lower likelihood of affluence.
energy_note: Not just poorer - less able to stop being poor.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the gradient is steeper for men at the bottom
description: The colorist mobility pattern differs by sex: the gradient penalising darker skin is steeper for men starting at the bottom of the origin distribution, while the gradient in persistence at the top is steeper for women.
energy_note: Steepest for exactly this dataset's subject.

aspect: EXAMPLE - measured several ways, including instruments
description: Evidence comes from PERLA (2010), INEGI's 2016 MMSI module, CEEY's 2017 EMOVI and ENADIS 2017. Solís, Güémez and Campos-Vázquez have benchmarked PRODER 2019 optical colorimeter readings against the PERLA palette, moving beyond interviewer classification. The PERLA project proposed the term pigmentocracy for the continent.
energy_note: Measured with an instrument, not an impression.

aspect: It is visible in advertising and casting
description: Who appears in Mexican television, advertising and politics is a daily public statement about which face belongs to which class, and a dark-skinned man sees it every day without it ever being said to him.
energy_note: Nobody says it. It is on every billboard.

aspect: The language of it is domestic and everyday
description: Güero, moreno, prieto, indio, naco, fresa - a dense everyday vocabulary for exactly the gradient DIS-001 measures, used affectionately, casually and as an insult, frequently by the same people in one conversation.
energy_note: A whole vocabulary for the thing nobody says exists.
